# Best portable power station for a CPAP

**My pick: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 (about $700).** It's a good all-rounder for a bedside backup. If you want to spend less, the Bluetti AC180 is the better value.

## Top picks

| Pick | Capacity | Nights (humidifier on / off) | Price |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** (best overall) | 1,024 Wh | ~1.7 / ~2.7 | ~$700 |
| **EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus** (expandable, whole-home backup) | 1,024 Wh, expands to 5 kWh | ~1.7 / ~2.7 | ~$719 |
| **Bluetti AC180** (best value) | 1,152 Wh | ~1.4 / ~3.1 | $499 |
| **EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus** (small and cheap) | 286 Wh | ~0.5 / ~0.8 | ~$299 |

- **Anker C1000 Gen 2:** Tested Watts rates it quietest (about 20 dB under 200 W). It has a 10 ms UPS switchover, so it takes over if the grid fails while you sleep. It also recharges fastest, in about 49 minutes. Its weakness is that it can't be expanded. ([Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/))
- **EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus:** It matches the Anker on capacity and UPS speed. You can add batteries later, for roughly eight humidifier-on nights at 5 kWh. It's also the heaviest of the four at 27.6 lb. ([Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/))
- **Bluetti AC180:** It's LiFePO4 with a 20 ms UPS. Dealectric lists it at $499, or **$474.05 with code AFF5OFF** (they tested it in Bluetti's cart on 2026-10-21). [Buy at Bluetti via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180). This is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you. Its UPS is slower than the Anker's and EcoFlow's. ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180))
- **EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus:** It's light at 10.4 lb and has a fast UPS. Treat it as a one-night, humidifier-off option. One source calls it "multi-night," but the others' math says under one night, so I'd trust the math. ([Outage Power Guide](https://outagepowerguide.com/reviews/best-power-station-for-cpap-machines/), [BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/))

I only have product-page links for the AC180. For the others, the review pages above link to retailers. BuyerSheet's table has "Check on Amazon" and official-store buttons for every model listed here. ([BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/))

## What to check before buying

- **Pure sine wave output** is non-negotiable for CPAPs. Every unit above has it.
- **Humidifier use:** A heated humidifier roughly doubles power draw, so it's the biggest factor in runtime. Sources assume different nightly use (about 520–720 Wh with humidifier), so measure your own machine with a cheap watt meter.
- **Sizing:** Use nightly Wh × nights ÷ 0.85. For two humidified nights, plan on about 1,200 Wh or more.
- **DC cord:** Your CPAP maker's 12 V DC cord skips inverter losses and adds roughly 10–20% runtime. Don't use a generic car adapter.
- **Jackery caveat:** The Explorer 1000 v2 is a good travel unit. But Jackery says its stations aren't recommended for medical devices, and it has a slower 20 ms UPS. Ask your CPAP maker before relying on one. ([Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/))
- **Air travel:** None of these can fly. They far exceed airline battery limits, so use a dedicated sub-100 Wh CPAP battery for flights.

This is general buying information, not medical advice. If you depend on CPAP, talk to your provider about a backup plan.

If you tell me your CPAP model and whether you use the humidifier, I can narrow it to one pick.
